questions.answer: Using the right-hand rule, \(\mathbf i\times\mathbf j=\mathbf k\), so the result is \((0,0,1)\).
This reverses \(\mathbf i\times\mathbf j\), so the result is \(-\mathbf k=(0,0,-1)\).

questions.prompt: Find the area of the parallelogram spanned by \((3,0,0)\) and \((0,4,0)\).
questions.answer: The cross product has magnitude \(|(0,0,12)|=12\). Hence the area is \(12\).

questions.prompt: Find the area of the triangle with sides \((2,0,0)\) and \((0,5,0)\) from one vertex.
questions.answer: The parallelogram area is \(|(0,0,10)|=10\). The triangle area is half of this, \(5\).

questions.prompt: Compute the torque \(\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F\) for \(\mathbf r=(2,0,0)\) m and \(\mathbf F=(0,3,0)\) N.
questions.answer: The cross product is \((0,0,6)\), so the torque is \(6\mathbf k\) N m.

questions.prompt: Test whether \((1,2,3)\) and \((2,4,6)\) are parallel using a cross product.
questions.answer: The second vector is \(2\) times the first, so their cross product is \(\mathbf0\). Therefore they are parallel.

questions.prompt: Find a vector perpendicular to \((1,1,0)\) and \((0,1,1)\).
questions.answer: Their cross product is \((1,-1,1)\), which is perpendicular to both input vectors.
The components are \((-1\cdot0-2\cdot1,2\cdot2-3\cdot0,3\cdot1-(-1)2)=(-2,4,5)\).
The cross product is \((2,3,-4)\). Its magnitude is \(\sqrt{4+9+16}=\sqrt{29}\).

questions.prompt: Find the unit normal to the plane spanned by \((1,0,1)\) and \((0,2,0)\).
questions.answer: The cross product is \((-2,0,2)\), with magnitude \(2\sqrt2\). A unit normal is \((-1/\sqrt2,0,1/\sqrt2)\).

questions.prompt: Compute \((\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\times(\mathbf j+\mathbf k)\).
questions.answer: Expand or use components \((1,1,0)\times(0,1,1)=(1,-1,1)\).

questions.prompt: Find \(k\) if \((1,2,3)\times(k,4,6)=\mathbf0\).
questions.answer: For zero cross product, the vectors must be parallel. Since \((k,4,6)=2(1,2,3)\), \(k=2\).

questions.prompt: Find the orientation sign of \((1,0,0)\times(0,1,0)\cdot(0,0,1)\).
questions.answer: The cross product is \((0,0,1)\), and its dot product with \((0,0,1)\) is \(1>0\). The orientation is positive.

questions.prompt: A triangular plate has vertices \(A=(1,0,2)\), \(B=(2,2,2)\), and \(C=(4,0,-1)\). Find its area and a unit normal vector.
questions.answer: Use side vectors \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(1,2,0)\) and \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(3,0,-3)\). Their cross product is \((1,2,0)\times(3,0,-3)=(-6,3,-6)\), with magnitude \(\sqrt{36+9+36}=9\). The triangle area is half the parallelogram area, so it is \(9/2\). A unit normal is \((-6,3,-6)/9=(-2/3,1/3,-2/3)\).

questions.prompt: Show that \((2,-1,1)\times(1,3,-2)\) is perpendicular to \((2,-1,1)\).
questions.answer: The cross product is \((-1,5,7)\). Dot it with \((2,-1,1)\): \(2(-1)+(-1)5+1\cdot7=-2-5+7=0\). A zero dot product shows it is perpendicular to \((2,-1,1)\).

questions.prompt: Find the sine of the angle between \((1,0,1)\) and \((0,1,1)\), then use it to find the area of the parallelogram they span.
questions.answer: The cross product is \((-1,-1,1)\), whose magnitude is \(\sqrt3\). Each input has magnitude \(\sqrt2\), so \(\sin\theta=|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b|/(|\mathbf a||\mathbf b|)=\sqrt3/(\sqrt2\sqrt2)=\sqrt3/2\). The parallelogram area is \(|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b|=\sqrt3\).

questions.prompt: For the triangle with vertices \(A=(0,0,0)\), \(B=(1,2,0)\), and \(C=(0,1,3)\), find a normal vector and decide which side of the triangle the point \(P=(6,-3,1)\) lies on relative to that normal.
questions.answer: Use \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(1,2,0)\) and \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(0,1,3)\). Their cross product is \(\mathbf n=(6,-3,1)\). To test \(P\), compute \(\mathbf n\cdot(P-A)=(6,-3,1)\cdot(6,-3,1)=36+9+1=46\), which is positive, so \(P\) is on the positive-normal side of the plane.

questions.prompt: A force \((0,5,0)\) N is applied at \((2,0,1)\) m. Find the torque about the origin, its magnitude, and explain whether the torque is perpendicular to the force.
questions.answer: Torque is \(\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F\). With \(\mathbf r=(2,0,1)\) and \(\mathbf F=(0,5,0)\), \(\boldsymbol\tau=(0\cdot0-1\cdot5,1\cdot0-2\cdot0,2\cdot5-0\cdot0)=(-5,0,10)\) N m. Its magnitude is \(\sqrt{(-5)^2+0^2+10^2}=5\sqrt5\) N m. Since \(\boldsymbol\tau\cdot\mathbf F=(-5,0,10)\cdot(0,5,0)=0\), the torque is perpendicular to the force.
